title: What on Earth uses space-fire research?
dek: Fire research on the station is meant to help life on the ground too. This story follows the few links the sources state, and marks that none of them names a product.
status_reason: Each observation comes from a NASA page, guide or paper. A product or a standard that changed because of this research is not covered by the sources we read.

beats.heading: A flame that dies on Earth, lives on the station

sentences.text: Cool flames have been produced on Earth, but they quickly flicker out.
On the station, cool flames can burn for minutes, giving scientists a better opportunity to study them.

beats.heading: Why that matters on the ground

sentences.text: The principal investigator of the CFI-G gas-flame experiment says cool flames are important to study because engine technology is trending toward lower temperatures.
Little is known about combustion chemistry at these temperatures, and experiments like CFI-G could help.
NASA's researcher guide says recent results from the BASS experiment indicate that the NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 screening test is not conservative.
Materials can burn at lower oxygen levels in microgravity than on Earth.
A product on Earth that came from this research is not covered by the sources we read.

limits: The engine link is the opinion of the principal investigator of CFI-G.
The cool-flame statement gives no number for how quickly the flames flicker out.
No sentence here is a verdict on any material, engine or item.
